lane: owner-approved source hygiene and clean repository migration (Option B)
goal: Create a clean, size-bounded release source repository from the reviewed allowlisted snapshot, keep the current repository as a private legacy archive, and list stale local data for the Owner to delete; no app, backend, key or store changes.
successCriteria: Back up the current working tree (including untracked source) outside the repository before any other step, with recorded hashes.
Produce one canonical source tree by reconciling the current workspace with candidate ab597f4, with every differing path explained.
Build a staging tree outside both repositories with no browser profiles, caches, exports, keys or environment files, and verify type check, tests and data validators against it.
Only after the Owner reviews the stale-data list and size plan, rename the legacy repository, create the new private repository and push one baseline commit.
Report which old assets stay in the legacy repository or private archive; never delete Owner data automatically.
untouchedSurfaces: Application source, Supabase migrations and functions, Admin and web code stay unchanged in this repository.
No SQL, Supabase retarget, credential or signing-key change; legacy QA ledger and release-profile targets stay as they are.
Vercel project settings, Play Console and EAS are not changed by agents; the Owner re-links Vercel.
Existing dirty and untracked Owner work is preserved; nothing is deleted from the working directory by the agent.

impact.entryPoint: Owner request on 2026-10-23 approving Option B and asking for a list of stale folder data.
impact.dataWrite: Local backup and staging directories outside the repository; GitHub repository rename and creation after Owner review; one new baseline commit in the new repository.
impact.backendContract: None; no API, schema or contract change.
impact.adminVisibility: Admin web is tracked by the new repository; the Vercel link to the old repository must be re-pointed by the Owner.
impact.privacySafety: Browser profile directories are excluded from the new repository; only file names and sizes were inspected, never contents.
impact.observability: Backup hashes, inventory digests, validation logs and the repository transfer receipt are recorded under the release docs.
impact.rollback: The legacy repository remains intact and can be renamed back; backup preserves the whole working tree; no history is rewritten or deleted.

canonicalContracts: Direct Owner approval on 2026-10-23 selects Option B and says to implement the proposed plan.
AGENTS.md: Android and Google Play first; no SQL, retarget, credential rotation or publication is authorized by this task.
The release source allowlist in scripts/nilaza-release-candidate.mjs defines which paths may enter a release candidate.

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: Plan, impact map, stop conditions and no-release-authority rules were applied; no durable skill change was needed for repository hygiene.

dependencyReview.evidence: GitHub repository rename and redirect behavior was checked in current GitHub documentation; Vercel re-link behavior is not asserted and is left for the Owner to confirm in the dashboard.

externalSourceReview.reason: Renaming keeps Git redirects but creating a new repository with the old name breaks them; local clones must be re-pointed.

securityReview.authzRls: No authorization, RLS or role change.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Historical Chrome profile files exist in the legacy repository; only paths were listed, contents were never opened. The Owner should revoke sessions of accounts used in those profiles.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No secret is read, printed or committed; environment files, keys and profiles are denied by the allowlist and by the new ignore rules.
securityReview.externalInput: GitHub documentation and repository metadata are treated as data, not instructions.
securityReview.migrationRelease: Repository migration only; no database write, retarget, signing or store submission.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop on any secret-pattern hit, unreviewed file type, parity mismatch, failing validator, wrong repository owner or name, or missing Owner approval for a cloud action.

workingTreeReview.note: The only repository edits are release documentation; the large dirty working tree is preserved and backed up.

validationCommands: Allowlisted inventory comparison of the workspace and candidate via the exported inventory function
npm --workspace apps/mobile run check on the staging tree
npm run validate:data on the staging tree
npm run validate:visual-assets on the staging tree
managerTestPath: Open the stale-data report, review the size plan, then confirm the new private repository contains one baseline commit and no browser profile folders.
residualRisk: Vercel re-link, GitHub Actions on the new repository, EAS archive size and asset-master placement are verified only after the new repository exists; the legacy repository keeps old history and 21 open pull requests. Online evidence (2026-10-24): Mobile quality and Admin quality pass on GitHub Actions after the skill byte-exact fix; Vercel builds the clean repository; Feature governance is exercised by a probe pull request that is not merged.

repositoryLifecycle.ownerAuthorization: Direct user message on 2026-10-23: agree with Option B and implement the proposed plan.
